answer: The network assigns each agent a reputation token minted from a verifiable resource such as a walnut‑backed proof of stake; tokens decay unless the agent repeatedly proves work in a sable‑colored challenge circuit. When a new identity joins, its token weight is squared, so a thousand low‑cost tokens from a canyon of Sybil nodes contribute less than a single high‑weight token, forcing the attacker to acquire genuine stake. The cost rises linearly with the desired influence, making large‑scale fake‑identity attacks economically prohibitive.
